newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope accepts resignation of scandal-stained bishop.
newsitem.headline: Pope accepts resignation of scandal-stained bishop.

text.p: Pope John Paul has accepted the resignation of a Sicilian archbishop who is on trial on charges of corruption and defrauding the European Union, the Vatican said in a statement on Saturday.
It said Archbishop Salvatore Cassisa had tendered his resignation when he turned 75 last December in accordance with Roman Catholic Church law, which obliges bishops to step down at that age.
The Pope has named Pio Vittorio Vigo, the bishop of the Sicilian town of Nicosia, to succeed Cassisa as archbishop of the town of Monreale just outside the island capital Palermo, the statement said.
Cassisa, one of the highest-ranking Catholic Churchmen ever to face Italian justice, went on trial last February.

He is charged with extortion and attempted extortion connected to bribes the prosecution says were demanded from construction companies and artisans seeking contracts for work on Monreale cathedral from 1990 to 1993.
The prelate is also accused along with two Sicilian agricultural inspectors of defrauding the European Union of some 200 million lire ($120,000).
Cassisa was once investigated for alleged Mafia ties but the case was dropped.
